1	# Custom shaders: colour contract, chunks and NaN safety (4.1)
2	
3	`material.custom({ glsl: { vertex, fragment } })` is the escape hatch for effects the
4	built-in materials do not cover (sky, water, energy, toon ramps). It has a colour
5	contract and three failure modes that cost real time on real GPUs. Chunk names and
6	signatures: `docs/api/glsl-chunks.md`.
7	
8	## Colour contract
9	
10	- A custom shader writes **linear light**. The output stage always sRGB-encodes it,
11	  and the default ACES operator tones it down further, so a hex colour written
12	  straight to `outColor` comes out greyer than authored (a day sky read grey for
13	  exactly this reason). Post effects are not the cause: bloom, grade, vignette and
14	  fxaa leave a custom shader's colour unchanged.
15	- To show a hex colour as authored: `#include <colorspace_decode>`, wrap the colour
16	  in `a3dSrgbToLinear`, and set `output: { toneMapping: "none" }` on the app.
17	  `<colorspace_encode>` provides `a3dLinearToSrgb` for the other direction.
18	- Any other tone-mapping operator still tone-maps custom colours; tune the exposure
19	  instead of compensating in the shader.
20	
21	## Chunks
22	
23	`#include <a3d_math>`, `<a3d_noise>`, `<a3d_sky>`, `<a3d_fog>`, `<a3d_triplanar>`,
24	`<a3d_toon>` and `<a3d_shadow>` are tested GLSL ES 3.00 helpers prefixed `a3d`. Use them instead of
25	pasting hashes, fbm, sky gradients or fog into every shader. Precedence when names
26	collide: built-in chunks, then these, t

- **Colour output:** Both shaders decode authored sRGB colours to linear. The app sets `output.toneMapping` to `"none"`, so the output stage only sRGB-encodes. This follows the colour contract in the Aura3D custom-shader docs.

I didn't add an island or any lights, because the two custom materials don't need them.
